newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp says euro can be as stable as mark.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp says euro can be as stable as mark.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday the European Union had made all necessary institutional preparations to allow the planned single currency to be as stable as the mark.

Krupp also said that in view of the success so far of nations' efforts to achieve monetary stability, it was likely that a "sufficient number" of nations would fulfil the inflation, interest rate and exchange rate criteria.
"There can be no doubt any more that all preparations have been made to help make the euro as stable as the mark," Krupp said in the text of a speech.
"Of course one has to keep working on stability. The Europeans have proven in recent years that they are determined to do so."

Krupp also reiterated that the Maastricht Treaty on European Union did not require exact adherence to the deficit criterion which states that a country's deficit must not exceed three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Referring to calls in Germany that any overshoot of the deficit above 3.0 percent should prevent a nation from qualifying for the single currency, Krupp said:
"If you look at the debate here, you get the impression that the stability success of monetary union depends on decimal points. This is not right."
Consolidating the state finances was necessary and overdue but could only be achieved with a medium-term plan which ensured lasting consolidation of the state finances.

"By contrast, hectically running after a specific deficit ratio does not improve the situation but leads to lower tax receipts and additional unemployment benefit payments and thereby worsens the situation. All this can be seen in Germany at the moment."
Krupp also said that the Treaty did not envisage a postponement of the planned January 1, 1999 launch date, adding that a delay made no economic sense.
